children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 16 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information about Alex. Since Alex is 16, I need to ask you an important question:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

(This could include things like staying in school, college, A-levels, or approved training programs)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education or training at the moment. He left school recently and he's signed up with the local careers service to help him figure out what to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is helpful to know. I have a few more questions to determine Alex's eligibility:

**When did Alex leave education or training - was it within the last 20 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it was fairly recent - definitely within the last 20 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Now I need to understand your current living situation:

**Do you live in the UK with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. We both live here in the UK together.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Has Alex started any paid work? And if so, is he working 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't started any paid work yet. He's just been focusing on sorting out his next steps with the careers service.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. One final question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why: Since Alex is 16 or 17 years old and has recently left education or training but registered with the local careers service, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for up to **20 weeks** from when he left education. This is a special provision for young people in Alex's situation.

**Important points to note:**

- This eligibility continues as long as Alex remains within the 20-week window from leaving education
- Alex has not started paid work of 24 hours or more per week
- Alex is not receiving benefits in his own right
- You both live together in the UK

**What happens after the 20 weeks?**

After the 20-week period ends, you would only continue to be eligible if Alex either:
- Returns to approved education or training, or
- Remains under 20 and enters approved education or training

If you have any other questions about your Child Benefit claim, please feel free to ask!
